destination.title: Axion origins, PQ protection and physical viability
destination.question: Under which model-dependent conditions can axion sectors arise, retain the required symmetry or gauge protection, and satisfy their intended particle-physics and cosmological roles?
destination.summary: A proposed broad family with a PQ-quality core and branches for ultraviolet constructions, flavor, cosmology, ultralight potentials and gauge consistency arguments. Numerical proximity supplies candidate membership only. Different systems, dimensions, mechanisms and historical phases remain distinguishable.

systems: String, extra-dimensional, supersymmetric and ordinary field-theory constructions
Adjacent electroweak axions, ultralight PNGBs and gauge-form descriptions
targets: Origin and hierarchy of symmetry-breaking and decay scales
Flavor, neutrino, dark-matter and cosmological compatibility
Conditional tests of gravitational contributions and consistency arguments
regimes: Invisible-axion, low-VEV and below-QCD breaking regimes
Specified cosmological histories and landscape assumptions
assumptions: Gravity-induced breaking, WGC, TCC and S-matrix arguments remain conditional and source-specific
Construction and viability claims are assessed as announced targets unless the supplied text supports more
Historical proposals remain accessible without becoming accepted premises
conventions: PQ-breaking VEVs, axion decay constants and anomaly-related multiplicities need not coincide
Anomalous gauge symmetries, anomaly-free gauge symmetries and residual global symmetries are distinguished
Fine singleton identity preserves the exact original source question, including compound targets
includes: Protection mechanisms and challenges to their sufficiency
Alternative axion masses, couplings and cosmological histories
excludes: A universal claim that gravity requires or destroys every axion mechanism
Equating common PQ vocabulary with fine question identity
Treating an eaten axion as a surviving physical axion
Current experimental certification or full-paper verification

sources.title: Open string axions and the flavor problem

evidence.text: Can minimal D-brane-inspired Froggatt–Nielsen flavor models produce an acceptable physical axion, with its decay constant inferred from quark hierarchies and neutrino-mass operators? The paper also asks what additional structure would be needed to address CKM mixing.

sources.title: On axionic dark matter in Type IIA string theory

evidence.text: Can a supersymmetric DFSZ axion sector be embedded in globally consistent Type IIA D6-brane Standard Models, with distinct string, Peccei–Quinn and electroweak scales, and a plausible hidden-sector origin for soft supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: The anomalous $U(1)_{\mathrm{anom}}$   symmetry and flavors from an SU(5) $\times $ SU(5) $'$ GUT in $\mathbf{Z}_{12-I}$ orbifold compactification

evidence.text: Can the residual anomalous heterotic U(1) supply both Peccei–Quinn and flavor symmetry in an explicit orbifold model, while producing light MSSM Higgs doublets, heavy colored partners and viable fermion mass textures?

sources.title: Axions in Type IIA Superstring Theory and Dark Matter

evidence.text: Can an intersecting-D6-brane quiver realize a flavor-dependent Peccei–Quinn symmetry with an open-string axion, relate its decay constant to fermion masses, and provide a possible dark-matter candidate through D2-instanton mass generation?

sources.title: Axions in a highly protected gauge symmetry model

evidence.text: Can an accidental global symmetry protected by an abelian gauge quiver yield a viable QCD axion or ultralight ALP dark matter? How are protection, the hierarchy between spontaneous-breaking and decay scales, and the colored fermions required for a QCD anomaly connected?

sources.title: An extension of the SM based on effective Peccei–Quinn Symmetry

evidence.text: Can an effective Peccei–Quinn symmetry protected by a gauge symmetry address the strong CP and domain-wall problems while also organizing fermion flavor, radiative neutrino masses, dark matter and leptogenesis?

sources.title: Is the magnitude of the Peccei–Quinn scale set by the landscape?

evidence.text: Can landscape selection determine an intermediate Peccei-Quinn scale in a gravity-safe supersymmetric axion model once both axion and neutralino dark matter are included, and what scale is preferred under alternative soft-term and relic-density assumptions?

sources.title: Inflection-Point Inflation with Axion Dark Matter in light of Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a gauged B−L extension with Peccei–Quinn symmetry realize TCC-motivated low-scale inflection-point inflation while accommodating axion dark matter, neutrino masses and baryogenesis?

sources.title: From Peccei Quinn symmetry to mass hierarchy problem

evidence.text: Can family-dependent U(1)X gauge charges and a global Peccei–Quinn symmetry jointly generate fermion mass textures, address strong CP, connect neutrino masses to the PQ scale, and give phenomenologically acceptable axion interactions?

sources.title: SMART U(1)$_X$ $-$ standard model with axion, right handed neutrinos, two Higgs doublets and U(1)$_X$ gauge symmetry

evidence.text: Can a U(1)X and Peccei–Quinn extension jointly accommodate neutrino masses, baryogenesis, axion dark matter, the strong CP problem and inflation, while avoiding axion domain walls and excessive isocurvature?

sources.title: $T′$ models with high quality flaxions

evidence.text: Can the gauged Peccei–Quinn mechanism protect a flavorful axion in a T′ flavor model against dangerous explicit PQ breaking, while retaining viable fermion textures and acceptable heavy-particle and axion phenomenology?

sources.title: Axion quality from the (anti)symmetric of SU($ \mathcal{N} $)

evidence.text: Can simple nonabelian gauge dynamics produce an accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry protected against sufficiently high-dimensional UV operators, while allowing colored relics to decay and yielding viable axion and heavy-relic dark matter?

sources.title: Scale and quality of Peccei-Quinn symmetry and weak gravity conjectures

evidence.text: Can one hidden gauge sector simultaneously protect an accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry against explicit breaking and explain its scale far below the Planck scale through a weak gravity conjecture? The paper also asks whether the resulting low-cutoff theory admits suitable axion cosmology.

sources.title: Variations on the SU(5) axion

evidence.text: How can axions and seesaw mechanisms coexist in non-supersymmetric minimal and flipped SU(5), and which apparent differences in fermion PQ charges affect low-energy axion phenomenology?

sources.title: A natural and simple UV completion of the QCD axion model

evidence.text: Can one simple ultraviolet model explain the origin, intermediate breaking scale and high quality of Peccei–Quinn symmetry while also stabilizing its extra dimension?

sources.title: Distribution of supersymmetry μ parameter and Peccei-Quinn scale fa from the landscape

evidence.text: How do landscape distributions of the supersymmetric μ parameter depend on the assumed solution to the μ problem, and can weak-scale anthropic selection also constrain the Peccei–Quinn scale in a gravity-safe PQ model?

sources.title: A QCD <math display="inline"><mi>R</mi></math>-axion

evidence.text: Can an anomalous supersymmetric U(1)R serve as the Peccei–Quinn symmetry, making the R-axion the QCD axion while maintaining viable gaugino masses, tuning the cosmological constant, and protecting axion quality?

sources.title: Hybrid SO(10) Axion Model without Quality Problem

evidence.text: Can an anomaly-free axial gauge extension of SO(10) generate an accidental PQ symmetry sufficiently protected against Planck-suppressed breaking, while supporting axion dark matter, realistic fermion masses and distinguishable axion couplings?

sources.title: High-quality axion from exact SUSY chiral dynamics

evidence.text: Can controlled supersymmetric chiral dynamics, perturbed by anomaly-mediated supersymmetry breaking (AMSB), produce a QCD axion while discrete gauge symmetries suppress gravitational PQ violation?

sources.title: Dark Matter and Strong CP Problem in Type IIA String Theory

evidence.text: Can an intersecting-D6-brane Type IIA construction supply axion/neutralino dark matter and embed a four-form mechanism for the strong CP problem, together with moduli stabilization and supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: Axions and a gauged Peccei-Quinn symmetry

evidence.text: Can extra-dimensional locality produce an accidental anomalous global Peccei–Quinn symmetry protected by a gauged U(1), while accommodating DFSZ or hadronic axions and correlated supersymmetry/PQ breaking scales?

sources.title: Stabilizing the axion by discrete gauge symmetries

evidence.text: Can discrete gauge remnants protect the Peccei–Quinn axion against Planck-suppressed symmetry violation, while realizing DFSZ and KSVZ models and linking the axion scale to supersymmetry breaking and the μ term?

sources.title: Stabilizing the axion and a natural solution to the mu problem of supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can a discrete gauge symmetry protect the axion's accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry against gravitational violations, while supersymmetric DFSZ dynamics relates the PQ scale to supersymmetry breaking and generates an electroweak-scale μ parameter?

sources.title: Axion models with high-scale supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Can approximately universal high-scale supersymmetry breaking accommodate a gravity-protected PQ solution, axion dark matter and gauge coupling unification, while relating the supersymmetry-breaking and PQ-breaking scales?

sources.title: Gravity and global symmetries

evidence.text: Can gravitational wormholes spoil the Peccei–Quinn solution of strong CP, can the dual two-form gauge symmetry protect the axion, and which modifications of short-distance gravity could suppress the dangerous effects?

sources.title: Open string axions and the flavor problem

evidence.text: Two anomalous matter-field redefinitions move the FN phase into currents and then remove the axion-gluon coupling. Current algebra determines nucleon couplings. Choosing Q_A=M_q⁻¹/(2 tr M_q⁻¹), with tr Q_A=1/2, removes axion–meson mass mixing; kinetic mixing remains suppressed.

sources.title: On axionic dark matter in Type IIA string theory

evidence.text: Use closed-polygon worldsheet selection rules for three-, four- and five-point superpotential interactions. Build F-, D- and soft-term potentials, then integrate out heavy vector and saxion degrees of freedom using scale separation.

sources.title: The anomalous $U(1)_{\mathrm{anom}}$   symmetry and flavors from an SU(5) $\times $ SU(5) $'$ GUT in $\mathbf{Z}_{12-I}$ orbifold compactification

evidence.text: Apply the imported ’t Hooft mechanism through phase counting and gauge/global generator mixing. Green–Schwarz-induced mixing removes one pseudoscalar direction; repeated breaking of anomaly-free gauge factors is used to retain a global direction.

sources.title: Axions in Type IIA Superstring Theory and Dark Matter

evidence.text: Use quiver charges and invariance of schematic operators y_f(φ/M_s)^{n_f}hff to constrain axion insertions. Chiral multiplicities are specified through oriented intersections I_{αβ}=Σ_α◦Σ_β; factorized-torus winding numbers are mentioned as a way to compute them.

sources.title: Axions in a highly protected gauge symmetry model

evidence.text: Use heavy-fermion triangle loops to generate anomalous and non-anomalous gauge couplings, and chiral field redefinitions to obtain derivative spin couplings. Gauge-anomaly cancellation constrains the permitted fermion content.

sources.title: An extension of the SM based on effective Peccei–Quinn Symmetry

evidence.text: Charge assignments determine anomaly coefficients and powers of S/M_* in effective Yukawa operators. Numerical diagonalization of the resulting mass matrices supplies illustrative quark and lepton spectra and mixing matrices.

sources.title: Protecting the Axion with Local Baryon Number

evidence.text: Can gauged baryon number protect an accidental PQ symmetry from dangerous Planck-suppressed operators while its anomaly-canceling exotic fermions implement the KSVZ hidden-axion mechanism?

sources.title: Strong-$CP$ with and without gravity

evidence.text: Does coupling QCD to gravity turn strong CP from a naturalness puzzle into a consistency condition requiring an exact axion mechanism, and can a gauge formulation protect that mechanism without a global Peccei–Quinn symmetry?

sources.title: Axion Landscape Cosmology

evidence.text: Can complex multi-axion landscapes supply cosmologically long-lived low-CC vacua, sufficient inflation after vacuum decay, and ultralight dark matter compatible with a Peccei–Quinn solution of the strong CP problem?

sources.title: Planck scale physics and the Peccei-Quinn mechanism

evidence.text: Can the Peccei–Quinn mechanism naturally solve the strong-CP problem when Planck-scale physics induces explicit global-symmetry breaking, and how would such breaking change axion phenomenology?

sources.title: Axion species scale and axion weak gravity conjecture-like bound

evidence.text: Can perturbative breakdown of axion–tower interactions define an axion species scale whose comparison with the gravitational species scale yields an axion-WGC-like bound, and what conditional consequences follow for black-hole PQ-charge reduction?

sources.title: Semiclassical gravity and invisible axions

evidence.text: Can calculable semiclassical gravitational instantons break Peccei–Quinn symmetry sufficiently to disturb the invisible-axion solution of strong CP, alter its spectrum, or change its cosmological problems?

sources.title: Natural Theories of Ultralow Mass PNGB's: Axions and Quintessence

evidence.text: Can a Wilson-line PNGB remain ultralight despite Planck-scale global-symmetry breaking and provide a natural axion or quintessence field, potentially with its tiny potential generated by Planck effects themselves?

sources.title: High-Quality Axions in a Class of Chiral U(1) Gauge Theories

evidence.text: Can chiral U(1) gauge theories produce accidental axions whose explicit symmetry breaking is sufficiently suppressed for quintessence, fuzzy dark matter, or a solution to the strong CP problem?

sources.title: Axionic domain wall number related to U(1)$_{\rm anom}$ global symmetry

evidence.text: Can an intermediate-scale QCD axion inherited from an anomalous string U(1) simultaneously address gravitational spoil of PQ symmetry and the cosmological domain-wall problem, despite an apparently large anomaly-related vacuum multiplicity?

sources.title: Mass generation for an ultralight axion

evidence.text: Can instantons of a gauge symmetry broken near the Planck scale generate an axion mass near 4×10^−33 eV, as required by the previously proposed ultralight-pNGB explanation of effective cosmological vacuum energy?

sources.title: Heavy fields and the axion quality problem

evidence.text: Can intermediate heavy fields amplify gravity-induced PQ breaking enough to undermine axion-quality estimates based solely on Planck-suppressed operators, even when gauge symmetries forbid low-dimensional breaking?

sources.title: Coloured gravitational instantons, the strong CP problem and the companion axion solution

evidence.text: Do coloured Eguchi–Hanson gravitational instantons generate a sufficiently large independent CP-violating axion potential to compromise the single-axion Peccei–Quinn mechanism, and can an additional axion cancel both sources?

sources.title: Tale of two- $U(1)$ axion models

evidence.text: How can elementary Peccei–Quinn and composite axial U(1) symmetries jointly cancel QCD and hidden-QCD CP phases, and what axion masses and photon couplings result? The axion quality problem motivates the classification.

sources.title: PQ axiverse

evidence.text: Can the Peccei–Quinn mechanism survive both high-energy QCD instantons and quantum-gravity contributions to the axion potential in a large ensemble of string compactifications?

sources.title: Peccei-Quinn symmetry with residual symmetries

evidence.text: Can a PQ symmetry with residual discrete subgroups produce an invisible axion from low, potentially TeV-scale scalar VEVs, suppressing its fermion couplings while avoiding the Higgs-portal tuning associated with a very high symmetry-breaking scale?

sources.title: Quintessence Axion Revisited in Light of Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can a concrete quantum-gravity model realize the proposed electroweak axion, Planck-scale decay constant, approximate symmetry protection, and preserved dark-energy potential amplitude simultaneously?

sources.title: Solutions to the strong CP problem in a world with gravity

evidence.text: Which strong-CP solutions survive hypothetical Planck-scale violations of global symmetries, and can gauge symmetries protect the Peccei–Quinn mechanism sufficiently?

sources.title: Accidental Peccei-Quinn symmetry from gauged U(1) and a high quality axion

evidence.text: Can an anomaly-free gauged axial U(1)a generate accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry while suppressing gravity-induced PQ violation sufficiently to preserve the strong-CP solution and viable axion dark matter?

sources.title: Hadronic axion, baryogenesis and dark matter

evidence.text: Can an extra Peccei–Quinn (PQ) symmetry preserve a primordial baryon asymmetry against electroweak sphalerons and lepton-number violation, including without an initial B−L asymmetry? How do hadronic and DFSZ axion models differ, and can the protecting charge connect baryons to dark matter?

sources.title: Quintessence Axion Revisited in Light of Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can a supersymmetric electroweak axion model retain B+L violation without unacceptable proton decay? The setup uses FN suppression and an R symmetry, together with TeV-scale supersymmetry breaking and the MSSM ultraviolet gauge coupling.

sources.title: GeV-scale QCD Axion

evidence.text: Can Peccei–Quinn breaking below the QCD scale solve strong CP while allowing a GeV-scale axion, avoiding existing constraints and producing observable hadronic or ultraviolet-completion signatures?

sources.title: Axion from pseudo Goldstone seesaw without Peccei-Quinn symmetry

evidence.text: The historical manuscript asks whether tiny mixing between heavy and ultralight pseudo-Goldstone bosons could produce an axion without an anomalous Peccei–Quinn global symmetry, while keeping symmetry-breaking scales near TeV.

sources.title: Can decaying particles raise the upper bound on the Peccei-Quinn scale?

evidence.text: How far can entropy from decaying coherent oscillations or nonrelativistic particles relax the cosmological upper bound on the Peccei–Quinn scale, while preserving primordial nucleosynthesis?

sources.title: High-Quality Axion Models with the Anomalous $U(1)_X$ Gauge Symmetry

evidence.text: Can an anomalous gauged U(1)X protect an accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry against dangerous Planck-suppressed operators using only two vector-like pairs, while permitting anomaly cancellation and approximate gauge coupling unification?

sources.title: Gravitational instantons and the quality problem of the QCD axion: Facts, speculations, and statements in between

evidence.text: Can gravitational instantons generate enough explicit Peccei–Quinn breaking to compromise the QCD axion, after accounting for fermion zero modes, loop factors, ultraviolet thresholds, and admissible gravitational boundary conditions?

destination.title: Charge storage and return
destination.question: Which conserved charges can black holes store and return, given available carriers, their lifetimes and the energy required for emission?
destination.summary: Organizes charge bookkeeping and species arguments while distinguishing hidden charge, exterior gauge flux and independently charged carriers.

systems: Black holes with species charges or other conserved charge labels
assumptions: Charge conservation and positive carrier energy costs apply only where specified
conventions: Independent binary charges and discrete gauge charges are not silently identified

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Can the charge-return argument survive if massive species decay, provided their lifetimes exceed the relevant black-hole evaporation time?

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: How much exactly conserved charge can a black hole store when each of N equal-mass species carries its own independent binary charge?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Can a black hole carrying one independent discrete gauge charge per species return all charges through thermal emission? The available energy at the emission threshold bounds the number of massive charge carriers it can emit.

sources.title: Cobordism Classes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which conserved charges are compatible with black-hole evaporation? Exterior gauge flux distinguishes gauge charges from charges hidden entirely behind the horizon.

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Couple a test string to the Stückelberg field strength through a boundary term and compare linked and unlinked histories. Their phase difference detects global hair despite vanishing local classical fields.

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Evaluate proposed constraints against controlled constructions and independently motivated infrared arguments, recording assumptions and construction quality. The review distinguishes complete worldsheet constructions from more assumption-dependent string-inspired models and treats their agreement as graded evidence.

sources.title: Cobordism Classes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Construct a quotient filling, place the asymptotic compactification at infinity, and transport it by T-duality. Compatible wrapping yields a filling for the product circle class.

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Estimate the gravitational kinetic correction from each field, add the contributions over species, and compare with the effective Planck coefficient. Equal characteristic scales yield an N-fold enhancement unless cancellations intervene.

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Store conserved charge in a black hole, identify when thermal emission can discharge it, and compare remaining mass with minimum recovery energy. Independent binary charges yield the species application; the scalar cascade demonstrates failure of naive unit-charge counting.

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Link scalars through successive cubic powers and eliminate the heavier n−1 fields. The reported interaction compresses cyclic order exponentially relative to field count while leaving high-charge carriers in the underlying spectrum.

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Can an exactly conserved charge have unlimited range if it creates no classical long-range field and returning it through available carriers has a nonzero energy cost?

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Can many Standard Model singlets have natural portal strengths while retaining a charge realization compatible with the black-hole hierarchy argument?

sources.title: The String landscape, black holes and gravity as the weakest force

evidence.text: How can weakly coupled charged black holes avoid leaving many stable Planck-scale charge labels?

destinations.title: Can the charge-return argument survive if massive species decay, provided their lifetimes exceed the relevant black-hole evaporation time?
How much exactly conserved charge can a black hole store when each of N equal-mass species carries its own independent binary charge?

Can a black hole carrying one independent discrete gauge charge per species return all charges through thermal emission? The available energy at the emission threshold bounds the number of massive charge carriers it can emit.
Which conserved charges are compatible with black-hole evaporation? Exterior gauge flux distinguishes gauge charges from charges hidden entirely behind the horizon.
